2026-08-05T04:12:40.0242511Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0243141Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0243482Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0243961Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0244379Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0244866Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0246414Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0248109Z >
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0250361Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0252900Z >
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0253699Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0254453Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0254638Z ### How to Use
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0254871Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0255562Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0256259Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0256445Z ```bash
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0256986Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0257708Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0258327Z ```
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0258547Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0258802Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0259331Z ```bash
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0259860Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0260641Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0261466Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0262192Z ```
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0262397Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0263206Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0264079Z ```bash
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0264628Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0265293Z ```
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0265492Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0265942Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0266531Z ```bash
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0267052Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0267892Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0268582Z ```
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0268783Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0269045Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0269462Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0270842Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0272393Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0272567Z ```bash
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0273190Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0274021Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0274835Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0275137Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0276432Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0277564Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0278369Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0278833Z ```
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0279036Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0279770Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0280652Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0280821Z ```bash
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0281512Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0282377Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0283438Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0283881Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0284285Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0285064Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0285603Z ```
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0285807Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0286004Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0286807Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0287757Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0288712Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0289706Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0290824Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0291359Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0291544Z ### Notes
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0291757Z 
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0292383Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0293987Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0295226Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0296472Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0297653Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0298757Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0299719Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0300419Z </mcp-clis>
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0300829Z <github-context>
2026-08-05T04:12:40.0301427Z The following GitHub context information is available for this workflow:
